chapters.name: Force and Motion
chapters.introduction: Force and motion is a foundational physics chapter covering Newton's three laws, types of force, speed, velocity, acceleration, and equations of motion.
chapters.whyItMatters: 10-12 marks. Numerical problems on equations of motion appear every year.

topics.name: Newton's Laws of Motion
topics.explanation: 1st Law (Inertia): An object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a net force. 2nd Law: F = ma. 3rd Law: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
keyPoints: F = ma is the most used formula
Action-reaction pairs act on different objects
topics.examTip: Always mention units in numerical answers (N, m/s², kg).
topics.formula:
F = ma
Acceleration a = (v-u)/t
v² = u² + 2as

topics.name: Equations of Motion
topics.explanation: Three kinematic equations relate initial velocity (u), final velocity (v), acceleration (a), time (t), and displacement (s). Use these for uniform acceleration problems.
topics.examTip: List all given values first, identify the unknown, then choose the right equation.
topics.formula: v = u + at ; s = ut + ½at² ; v² = u² + 2as

chapters.name: Work, Energy and Power
chapters.introduction: Chapter covers mechanical work, kinetic and potential energy, conservation of energy, and power calculations relevant to SEE.
chapters.whyItMatters: 8-10 marks. Conservation of energy is the most tested concept.

topics.name: Work and Energy
topics.explanation: Work = Force × Displacement × cos θ. Kinetic Energy = ½mv². Potential Energy = mgh. Law of conservation: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted.
keyPoints: Work is scalar despite F and d being vectors
topics.examTip: In conversion problems, set KE = PE to find velocity at a given height.
topics.formula: W = Fs·cosθ  ;  KE = ½mv²  ;  PE = mgh  ;  P = W/t

chapters.name: Light and Optics
chapters.introduction: Covers reflection, refraction, lenses (convex/concave), mirrors, and the human eye as an optical instrument.
chapters.whyItMatters: 8-10 marks. Lens formula and mirror formula numericals appear frequently.

topics.name: Reflection and Refraction
topics.explanation: Reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection. Refraction: light bends at interface. Refractive index n = sin i / sin r. Total internal reflection occurs when angle > critical angle.
keyPoints: Snell's Law: n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r
topics.examTip: Draw a diagram with normal line for full marks on optics questions.
topics.formula: n = sin i / sin r  ;  n = c/v

chapters.name: Electricity and Magnetism
chapters.introduction: Covers Ohm's law, series/parallel circuits, electrical power, magnetic effects of current, and electromagnetic induction.
chapters.whyItMatters: 10-12 marks. Circuit calculations are very common in SEE.

topics.name: Ohm's Law and Circuits
topics.explanation: Ohm's Law: V = IR. Series: R_total = R₁ + R₂; same current flows. Parallel: 1/R_total = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂; same voltage across each. Electrical Power P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
keyPoints: Power unit = Watt; Energy unit = Joule or kWh
topics.examTip: For mixed circuits, simplify parallel branches first, then add series.
topics.formula: V = IR  ;  P = VI = I²R  ;  E = Pt

chapters.name: Atomic Structure and Chemical Reactions
chapters.introduction: Atomic models (Bohr's), electron configuration, types of chemical reactions, and balancing chemical equations.
chapters.whyItMatters: 8-10 marks. Balancing equations and electron configuration appear every year.

topics.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
topics.explanation: Acids: pH < 7, turn blue litmus red, donate H⁺. Bases: pH > 7, turn red litmus blue, accept H⁺. Salts are formed by neutralisation. Indicators: litmus, phenolphthalein, methyl orange.
topics.examTip: Know the colour changes for all three indicators.

topics.name: Metals and Non-metals
topics.explanation: Metals: lustrous, malleable, good conductors, form basic oxides. Non-metals: poor conductors (except graphite), form acidic oxides. Reactivity series determines displacement reactions.
keyPoints: Reactivity series: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Cu, Ag, Au
topics.examTip: Higher in reactivity series = displaces lower metals from their salts.

chapters.name: Cell and Human Body
chapters.introduction: Cell structure (plant vs animal), body systems (digestive, respiratory, circulatory, nervous), reproduction and heredity.
chapters.whyItMatters: 12-15 marks. Diagrams with labels are required for many biology questions.

topics.name: Cell Structure
topics.explanation: Animal cell: cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes. Plant cell includes: cell wall, chloroplast, vacuole (large). Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound nucleus (bacteria).
topics.examTip: Draw a well-labelled diagram. Each correctly labelled part earns marks.

topics.name: Reproduction and Heredity
topics.explanation: Sexual reproduction: fusion of gametes, genetic variation. Asexual reproduction: budding, fragmentation, no variation. Heredity: DNA carries genes. Mendel's laws of inheritance apply to dominant/recessive traits.
keyPoints: Recessive: expressed only in homozygous state
topics.examTip: Use Punnett squares for cross problems — always show the working.

chapters.name: Environment, Ecosystem and Technology
chapters.introduction: Covers food chains, ecosystems, environmental degradation, renewable energy, and modern communication technology.
chapters.whyItMatters: 8-10 marks. Environmental questions are short-answer based and straightforward.

topics.name: Renewable Energy and Technology
topics.explanation: Renewable: solar, wind, hydro, biomass. Non-renewable: fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas). Nepal focuses on hydropower. Modern tech: internet, AI, satellite communication, mobile networks.
keyPoints: Solar energy is unlimited and pollution-free
Nepal has highest hydropower potential in the world
topics.examTip: Answer environmental questions with causes, effects, AND solutions for full marks.
